parsed.process: id retting: separating bast fibre from non-fibrous plant material by microbial/chemical degradation of pectin, then mechanical breaking and scutching
parsed.process_problem: Retting endpoint is judged by feel/experience; under-retting leaves fibres bound, over-retting weakens/dirties them; quality/timing vary by method and conditions, and no labeled per-batch endpoint dataset exists.
parsed.recent_technique: Hyperspectral foundation models (self-supervised, few-shot fine-tuning) -- e.g. SpectralEarth-pretrained backbone, HyperFM, SpecAware
parsed.how_it_improves: A close-range hyperspectral camera images retting stems/fibre bundles; reflectance cubes feed an SSL-pretrained HSI backbone fine-tuned on only a few dozen labeled stems (graded under-/optimally-/over-retted via tensile + cleanliness checks). The model learns the spectral signature of pectin/cementing-compound degradation and outputs a per-batch retting-completion score and 'harvest now' alert. This replaces feel/experience with an objective, repeatable endpoint readout, cutting both under-retting rework and over-retting fibre loss across pond/stream/field conditions.
parsed.why_recent_technique_beats_mature_approa: Mature hyperspectral+ML (Run-22) needs a large per-task labeled dataset to learn pectin-degradation spectra -- but the problem statement is that NO labeled per-batch endpoint dataset exists, so supervised models can't be trained. The HSI foundation model's SSL pretraining means the spectral-feature backbone is already learned; only a few labeled stems are needed to fine-tune, so label-efficient few-shot fine-tuning removes the exact no-large-dataset blocker that stops the mature method.
parsed.feasibility_now: Not drop-in. Requires (1) a close-range hyperspectral camera (hardware cost), (2) collecting a small labeled set of graded retted stems, and (3) bridging a real out-of-distribution gap: backbones are pretrained on satellite/airborne earth-observation HSI, not close-range wet-stem spectra, so transfer is plausible but unproven and may need domain-adaptive fine-tuning. MEDIUM maturity: the right tool, but the least drop-in of the candidates.

reasoning_trace.inputs_seen: the process (pectin-degradation retting + scutching) + its open problem (subjective endpoint, no labeled per-batch dataset) + HSIFM's label-efficient few-shot capability + its MEDIUM maturity tier
reasoning_trace.reasoning: Retting endpoint is fundamentally a chemical-state question (how much pectin/cement remains), which has a spectral signature -- a natural hyperspectral target. The blocker for ordinary hyperspectral ML is that no labeled per-batch endpoint dataset exists, so a supervised model can't be trained. HSI foundation models invert this: SSL pretraining supplies the backbone, and few-shot fine-tuning needs only a handful of graded stems, directly matching 'no large dataset.' Feasibility is realistic-not-optimistic because the technique still demands a hyperspectral camera and faces a genuine OOD gap from satellite/airborne pretraining to close-range wet-stem spectra.
reasoning_trace.decision: Use an SSL-pretrained HSI foundation model, few-shot fine-tuned on a few graded retted stems, as an objective per-batch retting-endpoint detector that flags optimal harvest time.
reasoning_trace.confidence: medium - MEDIUM tier reflects a real domain gap (EO-pretrained -> close-range stem spectra) and a hardware requirement, even though few-shot is the correct fit for the missing-dataset problem
reasoning_trace.could_be_wrong_if: the satellite/airborne-pretrained backbone fails to transfer to close-range wet-stem reflectance (OOD), or pectin-degradation state has no separable spectral signature at field-usable resolution, or the hyperspectral-camera cost is prohibitive for low-margin fibre operations.
